text:
sara: Heads up — after the staged rollout we’re seeing elevated latency + 502s for a subset of Dedicated traffic. Canary alarm fired but traffic didn’t fully drain. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary health degraded for deployment dply-20241203-18. Pager: @oncall-sre. Incident ID: INC-20241203-17. Link: https://redwood/incident/INC-20241203-17
oncall-sre: On it. grabbing list of affected pools and rollout id, assigning primary eng.
product-support: Noted. Any immediate customer-facing impact? which customers hit?
sara: Looks like 3 premium Dedicated customers, latency spike to ~1.6s p50 -> 4s p95 and ~8% 502s for long sequences. Not universal.
mike: Checking rollout metadata — id=dply-20241203-18, strategy=staged-10-25-100. Auto-rollback policy is set but I see no rollback event. Investigating why the arbiter didn’t trigger.
jen: Quick note: the feature-flag gate controlling canary drain was set to the wrong flag key in config (ff/dedicated_canary_v2 vs ff/dedicated_canary). Canary monitor didn't see the traffic marker so it never flipped drain.
eli: If that's the case we should do a manual traffic-weight revert + flip feature flag then run the rollback command from runbook. I can execute. What’s the rollback command again?
mike: Use the runbook snippet: ```
# revert to previous stable
redwoodctl rollout rollback --deploy-id dply-20241203-18 --to-image redwood/inference:v2.13.9 --confirm
```
sara: +1. Also flip the flag so the release path doesn’t re-enable the canary marker: ```
redwoodctl feature-flag set ff/dedicated_canary=false --env prod
```
eli: Executing now — flipping flag and initiating rollback. I’ll run smoke tests after the rollout completes and paste results. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: ACTION: oncall-sre initiated manual rollback (dply-20241203-18) at 2024-12-03T18:14:05Z.
eli: Rollback command output: ```
Initiating rollback to redwood/inference:v2.13.9
Draining 25% traffic -> 0% for pools: ded-pool-a, ded-pool-b
Scaling up stable instances, applying image
Rollback complete on 3/4 hosts; one host pending post-start checks
```
jen: I’m watching logs for the host that was pending. Looks like proxy config reload failed on host-7 due to stale cert path; restarting agent.
oncall-sre: I’ll take host-7 and restart the agent hook. tagging infra.
mike: Running quick smoke tests against stable image: ```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -d '{"input":"smoke test"}' | jq '.latency_ms'
# result: 84ms
```
sara: Nice. 502s trending down. Can we get a customer impact note ready? product-support please draft.
product-support: Drafting: "We identified increased latency and error rates for some Dedicated customers following a staged deploy. We’ve initiated a rollback to the previous stable version and flipped a release gate. Systems are recovering; we will follow up with a root cause."
product-support: Posting to affected customers and support channels now.
eli: host-7 agent restart fixed the last host, all hosts healthy. Post-rollback smoke: p50=90ms p95=260ms 502s ~0.5% (baseline 0.3%).
jen: Marking deploy dply-20241203-18 as failed, setting tag rollback-executed, kicking off a postmortem runbook step to capture the flag mismatch.
sara: Good job. Next: set follow-up action items: (1) fix flag naming validation in CI, (2) add a canary metric that watches the correct traffic marker, (3) customer RCA timeline.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: INC-20241203-17 marked resolved at 2024-12-03T18:20:50Z by oncall-sre. Duration ~8 minutes.
sara: Thanks all — handover to postmortem owners jen + product-support. Closing live coordination channel. :pray:
